summary: This resolution declares the Equal Rights Amendment validly ratified as part of the Constitution, overriding its original 1972 deadline, on the grounds that three-fourths of the states have approved it.

scores.thoughts: The bill text is a joint resolution solely declaring the Equal Rights Amendment ratified by removing the time limit. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or implications related to federal spending levels or budgets.
The resolution addresses only constitutional ratification of the ERA and has no language concerning tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No engagement with healthcare systems, coverage models, or market structures appears in the bill text.
The bill is unrelated to firearms regulations or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions or references to immigration policy, borders, or pathways exist in the text.
The bill text limits itself to ERA ratification mechanics and does not address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No connection to military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces appears.
The resolution contains nothing related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No references to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net expansions or reductions.
The bill does not engage with education funding, school choice, or federal involvement in schools.
No content related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The text has no bearing on sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
Unrelated to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization measures.
No fiscal policy, deficit, or debt-reduction language is present.
The bill text is confined to procedural ratification of the ERA and does not directly expand or limit legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concerning foreign assistance or international aid.
The resolution does not address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No engagement with technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill contains no references to worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The text is strictly about ERA ratification timing and does not prioritize civil rights enforcement versus religious exemptions.
